quotes: "Calliope is a virtual reality (VR) system that enables users to explore and manipulate generative design solutions in real time." (p. 1)
"To account for the above design considerations, we developed Calliope: a user-driven interface for tight-looped human-AI creative collaboration within a virtual environment [Figure 2]." (p. 4)

"Our walkthrough tasks were completed by members of the research team and chosen in order to demonstrate the variability of design approaches supported by Calliope, as well as the application of our design considerations mentioned previously." (p. 6)

"These results are, of course, hardware dependent and should be explored further to better understand the computation demands of performing multiple optimization tasks in parallel with one another and a complex VR authoring system." (p. 8)

quotes: "This process not only allows Calliope to perform mutation on a user-manipulated object, but also automates several aspects of the sculpting process by cleaning the designers manipulated mesh, thus mitigating the time required for careful mesh manipulation by the user and enabling a more rapid sculpting process." (p. 8)

claim_entries.value: Calliope enables real-time VR exploration and manipulation of generative solutions while using computational idle time for parallel embodied exploration and tight human-in-the-loop collaboration (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "Calliope accounts for the typical idle times in the generative design process by using a virtual environment to encourage parallelized and embodied data-exploration and synthesis, while maintaining a tight human-in-the-loop collaboration with the underlying algorithms." (p. 1)

claim_entries.value: feasibility
artifact
working_system_evaluated — the implemented system received a computational stress test (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "To examine this, we stress-tested our system." (p. 8)

claim_entries.value: Forte is identified as the closest predecessor for iterative 3D-printable-object design through topology-optimization interactions (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "Most closely related to our work is Forte, which allows a user to iteratively design 3D printable objects using interaction techniques designed for topology optimization [8]." (p. 3)

claim_entries.value: single-operation and simultaneous-operation idle times were recorded for generation, mutation, and mesh interpretation; parallel generation was omitted because its added latency was negligible (PDF p. 11).
quotes: "To evaluate this, we performed 2, 3, and 4 operations simultaneously and recorded the idle time." (p. 11)

claim_exceeds_evidence

implementation and timing tests support technical feasibility, but the collaborative and user-engagement claims rely on research-team demonstrations rather than evaluation with target designers (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "Our walkthrough tasks were completed by members of the research team and chosen in order to demonstrate the variability of design approaches supported by Calliope, as well as the application of our design considerations mentioned previously." (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: generative 3D-object design in virtual reality (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "In this paper, we present Calliope (named for the Grecian muse of architecture and epic poetry) an interactive model synthesis and exploration tool that helps designers explore divergent solutions to a given design problem within a virtual environment." (p. 2)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — the support helps designers conduct the current design iteration and produce additional objects (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "The designer can then continue the design iteration process by generating and manipulating additional objects." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: mixed_or_transitioning — formative participants already knew generative design, while the proposed interface is also positioned as accessible to novices (PDF pp. 3, 9).
quotes: "Participants were familiar with generative design through their creative practice or professional development experience." (p. 3)

"The benefit of this metaphor-based approach could provide an accessible platform for novice users of generative design and democratize the design process as a whole by providing an intuitive interface for novice users to sample from generative solution spaces, and guide them through the iterative design process by encouraging gradual solution space constraints." (p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: strategy_or_process_gap — the interface structures how a designer narrows and makes sense of an otherwise daunting solution space (PDF p. 9).
quotes: "Therefore, interfaces to such algorithms must account for this by gently guiding the user through a process of iterative constraint and need-finding." (p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: process — the technical study measures time within single and parallel generative-design operations (PDF p. 11).
quotes: "In order to understand the idle time for each operation (mutation, interpretation of mesh editing, and generation) we first performed a series of each task sequentially." (p. 11)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — the radial environment supplies an explicit guide for iterative solution development (PDF p. 9).
quotes: "Our system used a radial-data visualization inspired environment in order to provide a structural guide for a user to iteratively develop design solutions." (p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: contingency — generated support responds directly to the geometry the designer edits (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "Calliope will take the user’s manipulated object as input, and attempt to create similar designs to the user’s custom input." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: distributed_support — designer evaluation and generative computation operate as complementary parts of an iterative dialogue (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "This approach facilitates an iterative design process, while encouraging a collaborative dialogue between the machine and designer." (p. 2)

paper_code_entries.value: generative_non_llm — candidate geometry is generated by a 3D generative adversarial network (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "We follow the architecture described by Wu et al. to produce a generator which creates a representation of a 3D object by randomly sampling a z vector from a probabilistic latent space." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: pre_llm_ai — the support path is a trained 3D GAN rather than an LLM or foundation model (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "Generative Adversarial Networks are appealing designers due to their promising ability to persistently generate novel objects [31]." (p. 8)

limitations: "While system development was largely guided by our formative interviews and literature review, we acknowledge that this is only one possible instantiation of the higher-level concepts and design goals." (PDF p. 4)
"We should note that after 4 parallel operations, performing direct mesh-editing incurred significant performance latency, which could cause motion sickness." (PDF p. 8)

"These results are, of course, hardware dependent and should be explored further to better understand the computation demands of performing multiple optimization tasks in parallel with one another and a complex VR authoring system." (PDF p. 8)
"Striking a balance between number of samples to present to the user is a significant challenge that hinges on constraints afforded by hardware and user bandwidth." (PDF p. 9)

"In a virtual environment, however, the displayed results are more easily inspected visually, but may be more difficult to group or explore based on parametric characteristics evident in 2D GUI interfaces for generative design [36, 41]." (PDF p. 9)

"While our system was able to generate and mutate between 4 different classes, additional object classes can be incorporated given adequate training of the network on a sufficient corpus of voxel object data." (PDF p. 9)
boundary_conditions: "Our walkthrough tasks were completed by members of the research team and chosen in order to demonstrate the variability of design approaches supported by Calliope, as well as the application of our design considerations mentioned previously." (PDF p. 6)
"Our virtual environment was developed in Unity 2019.3.0f6 using OpenGL 4.5 on Ubuntu 18.04, and tested on Vive Pro VR headset." (PDF p. 8)

"While our work focused on virtual reality, future work could expand this embodied data synthesis and exploration paradigm to augmented reality by allowing users to generate and manipulate objects in their physical environment." (PDF p. 9)

"Finally, while we focused on interfacing to generative adversarial networks in this paper, future work could extend using VR as an interface to other methods of generative design such as topological optimization." (PDF p. 9)
cards.claim: Calliope enables real-time VR exploration and manipulation of generative solutions while using computational idle time for parallel embodied exploration and tight human-in-the-loop collaboration

paper_code_entries.value: glider-flight traffic awareness and collision avoidance. (PDF p. 1)
quotes: "In this paper, we present an XR intelligent interface, GlideRX, to help pilots manage traffic awareness and prevent mid-air collisions." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — support is for managing present traffic and preventing imminent collision, not for instruction. (PDF p. 1)
quotes: "It allows for better support of situational awareness with respect to current collision warning systems currently available for gliders." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: mixed_or_transitioning — the intended and evaluated users include expert pilots and a student pilot. (PDF p. 10)
quotes: "The first was a preliminary user study with expert glider pilots to understand how real pilots could benefit from using GlideRX for their flying activities." (p. 10)
"One of them was a student pilot." (p. 10)

paper_code_entries.value: coordination_or_memory_gap — pilots must combine several changing traffic variables while controlling the aircraft, which the paper describes as daunting. (PDF p. 7)
quotes: "Asking pilots to consider them by themselves could be a daunting task." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: process, artifact — the paper measures visual acquisition and awareness processes as well as trajectory-prediction performance. (PDF pp. 8, 15)
quotes: "Figure 7 shows the plot of the performance of our model in predicting the state vectors for the next 11 seconds given the past 20 seconds state vectors." (p. 8)

"Concerning situational awareness, the results in Figure 16 support our hypothesis that all our alerting methods (visual cues) allow us to lower the participants’ error in their guess of the altitude and heading." (p. 15)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring, contingency, adaptation — four risk phases organize the support, and the visible information changes with the detected traffic risk. (PDF pp. 6, 10)
quotes: "Given these requirements, our solution organizes the possible threat scenarios into three main phases: low threat, moderate threat, and severe threat." (p. 6)
"The morphing speed between visual cues depends on the current risk level experienced." (p. 10)

paper_code_entries.value: non_generative_ai — an LSTM predicts traffic trajectories that determine the cues and risk response. (PDF p. 8)
quotes: "As anticipated in the design section, GlideRX implements a machine learning algorithm to compute the trajectories of all the traffic in the pilot’s glider surrounding area, including its own." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: pre_llm_ai — the scaffold’s meaning comes from non-generative trajectory prediction plus deterministic collision and display logic. (PDF p. 8)
quotes: "The model implements an Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network." (p. 8)

limitations: "These answers suggest that the currently implemented proposed visual cues present the lowest performance only for the head-tail trajectory geometry where the other traffic is in a blind spot of the pilot’s view while providing advantages for the remaining geometries." (p. 16)
"While the current implementation of the user interface supports the pilot also in the case of multiple intruders in low and moderate threat phases." (p. 16)
"Analogous support in the severe threat phase could be introduced in future releases, conditioned to meeting the attentional requirements of such a situation." (p. 16)

"While GlideRX usage in supporting pilots does not pose any specific ethical concern, providing instead aids and benefits to them, we identify the needs in its application to additionally guarantee (i) security of the AI model used for trajectory prediction against cyber-attacks (e.g., poisoning attacks); (ii) protection of XR technology against attacks on the visor itself [11] which can trick the pilot during sensitive maneuvers." (p. 16)
boundary_conditions: "The test was conducted among a group of seven people, six males and one female." (p. 10)
"One of them was a student pilot." (p. 10)
"The participants of this study were seven, different from the preliminary expert evaluation participants." (p. 15)
"One of the six participants did not take part in the situation awareness questionnaire, providing data only for the visual acquisition assessment." (p. 15)
"Further evaluation could also consider more complex flying scenarios, such as thermal soaring and competitive flying, where a larger population of pilots is involved simultaneously." (p. 16)
cards.notes: - The paper contains a preliminary single-condition usability evaluation and a separate repeated-condition task study, but `study_design` accepts one value; coded `within_subject` for the claim-bearing task study, losing the preliminary study’s distinct design.
cards.work_domain: glider-flight traffic awareness and collision avoidance
cards.claim: GlideRX improves pilots’ collision-avoidance capability through transient visual cues linked to risk phases
